entities.summary:
Beyond Good and Evil is a foundational text of modern philosophical thought, published in 1886 by German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche. This provocative book challenges traditional morality and explores the complexities of human existence.

Nietzsche's work was influenced by the cultural and intellectual currents of late 19th-century Europe, particularly the rise of positivism and the decline of Christian morality.

The publication of Beyond Good and Evil marked a significant turning point in Nietzsche's career, as he established himself as a major figure in the development of modern philosophy.

In the centuries that followed, Beyond Good and Evil has had a profound impact on intellectual and cultural discourse, influencing thinkers from Martin Heidegger to Jean Baudrillard.

The book's central theme – the tension between individual creativity and the forces of conformity – continues to resonate with contemporary audiences, making it a work of enduring relevance and significance.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "Beyond Good and Evil: Prelude to a Philosophy of the Future (German: Jenseits von Gut und Böse: Vorspiel einer Philosophie der Zukunft) is the philosophical work of Friedrich Nietzsche (1844–1900), published in 1886 — the most systematic and comprehensive presentation of his mature philosophy, written after Thus Spoke Zarathustra and intended as a critical demolition of the philosophical tradition from Plato through Kant in preparation for a new, honest philosophy that would affirm the will to power and the creation of new values. In nine parts covering 296 aphorisms and a concluding poem, it attacks philosophical dogmatism, the illusions of objective morality, the slave morality of Christianity and democracy, the philosopher's self-deception about the source of his values, and the decadence of 19th-century European culture — while sketching a positive vision of the philosopher as legislator of values, the noble as affirmer of life, and the possibility of a new, aristocratic philosophy beyond the 'good and evil' of conventional morality.

Nietzsche's key moves in Beyond Good and Evil include: his attack on the 'will to truth' as itself a moral assumption that requires philosophical examination ('Supposing truth is a woman — what then?'); his genealogical critique of philosophical systems as expressions of philosophers' drives and prejudices rather than disinterested pursuit of truth; his distinction between master morality (the noble affirmation of one's own power and vitality) and slave morality (the resentment of the powerful, dressed up as moral virtue); his critique of democracy and nationalism as herd phenomena; and his sketch of the 'free spirit' and the 'philosopher of the future' who will legislate new values for humanity. The work is written in Nietzsche's characteristic aphoristic, polemical style — brilliant, provocative, and deliberately combative.

Beyond Good and Evil's influence on 20th-century thought has been enormous and contested: its critique of conventional morality influenced existentialism (Heidegger, Sartre), poststructuralism (Foucault, Derrida), and critical theory; its distinction between slave and master morality was grotesquely appropriated by Nazi ideology (though Nietzsche himself was a fierce anti-nationalist and anti-antisemite); and its positive vision of self-creation, affirmation, and the will to power has been read as both an aristocratic ethic of excellence and a fascist legitimation of domination.", "subjects": ["Philosophy", "Modern Era", "Nietzsche", "Ethics", "Political Philosophy", "19th Century", "Continental Philosophy", "Existentialism"], "frameworks": ["STRUCTURAL_ANALYSIS", "CAUSE_AND_EFFECT"], "historicalSignificance": {"significanceScore": 7, "significanceNarrative": "Beyond Good and Evil remains one of the most widely read and influential philosophical works of the modern era, shaping our understanding of human nature and morality.", "significanceCategory": "regional"}, "_editLog": [{"timestamp": "2026-05-20T05:36:46Z", "editorId": "ollama/llama3.2:3b·local·manasa151-MS-7C56", "field": "summary", "oldValue": "Book by philosopher friedrich nietzsche Created by Friedrich Nietzsche.", "newValue": "
